preconditions.description: t is an integer representing the number of test cases, where 1 ≤ t ≤ 10⁴.

preconditions.expression: all(n.is_integer() and 2 <= n <= 2*10**5 and n % 2 == 0 for n in [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit()])
preconditions.description: Each test case starts with an even integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 2·10⁵), representing the number of dominoes.

preconditions.expression: all(len(dominoes) == n for n, dominoes in zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit()], [stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+1+n] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)]))
preconditions.description: Each test case contains exactly n dominoes, each represented as a pair of integers (aᵢ, bᵢ) where 1 ≤ aᵢ, bᵢ ≤ n.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(a) <= n and 1 <= int(b) <= n for line in stdin.splitlines() for a, b in [line.split()[:2]] if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit())
preconditions.description: Each domino pair (aᵢ, bᵢ) consists of integers between 1 and n (inclusive).

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_line.strip().upper() in ['YES', 'NO'] for stdout_line in stdout.splitlines() if stdout_line.strip())
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either 'YES' or 'NO' (case-insensitive), indicating whether the dominoes can be divided into two sets where all numbers in each set are distinct.

postconditions.expression: all((stdout_line.strip().upper() == 'YES') == (any(all(a != b for a in set_a) and all(a != b for a in set_b) for set_a, set_b in partition_dominoes(dominoes)) if dominoes else True) for dominoes, stdout_line in zip([[(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in line.split()[:2]] for line in stdin.splitlines() for _ in range(int(line.split()[0])) if line.strip().isdigit()], stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: The output 'YES' is correct if and only if there exists a partition of the dominoes into two sets where all numbers in each set are distinct. 'NO' is correct otherwise. The partition is defined as a split of dominoes into two disjoint subsets (set_a, set_b) such that all numbers in set_a are unique and all numbers in set_b are unique.
